To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a relativistic optical potential model of the pion emission function, which includes both strong radial flow and pion absorption, is able to describe the HBT and pion spectra from Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV/nucleon.
the DWEF model is capable of simultaneously reproducing the pion spectrum, the pion HBT radii and the elliptic flow of pions from central-collision RHIC Au+Au data at Os =200 GeV.
we have developed the first relativistic optical model for the emission function and applied it successfully to RHIC data, including a prediction of HBT radii for Cu+Cu collisions at RHIC energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the emission of particles from a dense, strongly interacting medium.
the study of the properties of strongly interacting matter at the highest energy densities.
the study of the space-time structure of the hadronization process in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the distorted wave model provides a very good description of the STAR HBT and pion data, and that the model is consistent with the idea of strong radial flow, and the presence of significant final-state interactions.
the DWEF calculations of HBT and spectra are in good agreement with the STAR Au+Au data at 200 GeV and that the DWEFs provide an excellent fit to the pion data over the entire range of centralities.
the distorted-wave emission function (DWF) model is a viable alternative to the standard hydrodynamical approach to the analysis of HBT and spectra data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a relativistic optical potential is needed for a realistic description of the pion emission from a hot and dense system of hadrons.

we have developed and applied a new model for the description of pions emitted from a strongly-interacting medium, and have shown it can describe both HBT correlations and spectra in a consistent way.
the distorted wave emission function (or distorted wave approximation) model is a powerful tool in the analysis of the HBT radii and spectra from heavy ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DWEF model is a powerful new tool for studying the space-time evolution of the system produced in high energy heavy-ion collisions.
the HBT radii are strongly correlated with the mean transverse momentum, which is in turn strongly correlated with the average number of collisions per particle, Ncoll.

a single model, which is tuned to fit the HBT and the pion spectra, can be used to describe the pion HBT data from a wide range of centralities, and that the HBT radii are consistent with a simple blast wave model of the pion emission source.
